s1.title: What If You Remembered Every Second?

beats.line: Imagine never forgetting a single page you read.
Every argument and date stored in razor-sharp detail.
What if you remembered every second?
Friends think it's cool—until mistakes replay forever.
Forgetting isn't a bug. It keeps you sane.

s2.title: How Honeybees Dance to Share GPS

beats.line: A scout bee finds flowers and races straight home.
Inside the hive, the whole crew gathers close.
She dances a figure-eight angled toward the sun.
Her waggle encodes exact distance and direction.
The squad launches straight to nectar—zero GPS needed.

s3.title: How GPS Finds You With Light Speed

beats.line: Thirty-one GPS satellites beam timestamps at light speed.
Your phone measures nanosecond delays from four satellites.
Where four spheres intersect, your position locks in.
Without Einstein's relativity, GPS drifts eleven kilometers daily.
Pure math and light speed within three meters.

s4.title: Why 3nm Chips Pack Billions of Transistors

beats.line: A hair is eighty thousand nanometers—chip gates are three.
Shrinking to three nanometers packs five times more switches.
Shorter signals slash wasted power and heat.
Engineers stack vertical fins like microscopic skyscrapers.
One hundred billion switches flipping billions of times.

s5.title: Why Flamingos Are Actually Born Grey

beats.line: Baby flamingos hatch completely fluffy and grey.
Their neon pink colour comes purely from diet.
Brine shrimp and algae carry bright red-orange carotenoids.
Enzymes break them down, dyeing growing feathers coral pink.
In nature, you literally are what you eat.
